**What changed**
- `assets/orders_clean.sql`: the source column `customer_id` used to be renamed to `cust`; now it keeps its original name. The `not_null` check now runs on `customer_id`.
- `assets/customer_revenue.sql`: the key, the selected column and the `GROUP BY` all use `customer_id`.
- No other files in the project used `cust`.

**Checks**
- `croft validate` found no problems.
- The preview matched the live tables: same rows, only the column name changed.
- `croft run orders_clean customer_revenue` succeeded and all checks passed:
  - `orders_clean` has 12 rows across 5 customers.
  - `customer_revenue` has 5 rows.
  - The dollar totals match in both tables: 373 = 373.
- `croft status` shows all four assets as ok.

Anything outside this project that queries `cust` from these tables (dashboards, saved queries, apps) will break and needs to use `customer_id` now.

**Nothing needs your approval.** One command was blocked early on: a read-only command that combined listing files and printing them, which needed approval. I used the file tools instead, so nothing was skipped.

score.finalMessage:
`daily_revenue` is fixed and rebuilt. It now shows **$118.00 from 3 orders on 2026-09-18**, which matches your payment dashboard.

**Cause:** `assets/daily_revenue.sql` joined each paid order to its line items before adding things up. That repeats an order once for every product line in it. So `count(*)` counted line items, not orders, and each order's total was added once per line. On 9/18, order 112 has 2 lines and order 114 has 3, so 3 orders became 6 and $118 became $273. The `items` column was already right, because it adds up quantity per line.

**Fix:** the query now totals the item quantities for each order first, then joins that one row per order. I also made it a `LEFT JOIN`, so a paid order with no line items would still count toward orders and revenue. No such orders exist today.

**Checked:** every day now matches a count and revenue total taken straight from `shop_orders`. Items per day are unchanged, and both checks pass.

| day | orders (was) | revenue (was) |
|---|---|---|
| 09-15 | 2 (3) | $58.00 ($92.00) |
| 09-16 | 2 (5) | $72.50 ($199.50) |
| 09-17 | 3 (6) | $79.00 ($158.00) |
| 09-18 | 3 (6) | $118.00 ($273.00) |
| 09-19 | 2 (3) | $45.50 ($78.50) |

Every past day was overstated, so any reports built from the old numbers were too high.

The change to `assets/daily_revenue.sql` is saved but not committed.

**Needs your approval:** nothing. The only command I ran that changes data was `croft run daily_revenue`, which rebuilds the table from the raw data and isn't on the ask-first list.

diff --git a/assets/daily_revenue.sql b/assets/daily_revenue.sql
index 7be05ca..3610639 100644
--- a/assets/daily_revenue.sql
+++ b/assets/daily_revenue.sql
@@ -1,11 +1,17 @@
 -- description: Paid orders, revenue (dollars) and items sold per day
 -- key: day
+-- Items are summed per order before the join: joining line items directly
+-- repeats each order once per line and inflates orders and revenue.
 SELECT
   o.order_date AS day,
   count(*) AS orders,
   sum(o.total_cents) / 100.0 AS revenue,
-  sum(i.quantity) AS items
+  coalesce(sum(i.items), 0) AS items
 FROM shop_orders o
-JOIN shop_order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id
+LEFT JOIN (
+  SELECT order_id, sum(quantity) AS items
+  FROM shop_order_items
+  GROUP BY order_id
+) i ON i.order_id = o.id
 WHERE o.status = 'paid'
 GROUP BY o.order_date
